rows.selection_reason: With no prior evidence, the most critical uncertainty is establishing a reliable performance baseline for the RNA modality before exploring more complex designs. config_001 (rna_only, singleprofile, pca_n2000) is the simplest RNA configuration: PCA-2000 is a fast, well-understood linear encoder, and singleprofile avoids confounding from aggregation choices. This experiment isolates the raw signal strength of the RNA modality under minimal modeling assumptions. It serves as a reference floor: if RNA alone performs well, subsequent experiments can test whether multiprofile aggregation, learned encoders (scvi, scgpt), or multimodal fusion add value; if it performs poorly, I can pivot toward image-only or multimodal configurations. Choosing the simplest valid baseline first avoids overcommitting to a complex architecture before knowing whether the underlying signal is informative, and it maximizes the interpretability of all 9 remaining experiments by giving a clean anchor point for comparison.

With only one completed experiment (config_001: rna_only, singleprofile, pca_n2000 → 48.5% acc), the most critical uncertainty is whether the image modality carries independent predictive signal. Before investing the remaining 8 experiments in multimodal fusion configurations, I need a clean image-only baseline. config_010 (image_only, singleprofile, resnet50) isolates the image contribution using a standard encoder and the same singleprofile setting as the RNA baseline, so the comparison is controlled. If image-only substantially outperforms or underperforms RNA-only, it reshapes which modality to prioritize in multimodal fusion and whether a stronger image encoder (ViT-L) or learned RNA encoder (scvi/scgpt) is the higher-value next step. This single experiment maximally reduces uncertainty about the modality landscape with minimal confounding changes.

Evidence: config_001 (rna_only, singleprofile, pca_n2000) achieved 48.5% accuracy, while config_010 (image_only, resnet50) was only 20.8%, establishing RNA as the dominant signal and resnet50 image as weak. The biggest uncertainty is whether the RNA representation itself can be improved. This experiment tests scvi_n200 (a learned, denoised VAE-based representation) versus pca_n2000 (linear) while holding model_setting=rna_only and profile_setting=singleprofile constant, isolating the effect of the RNA encoder. If scvi_n200 improves meaningfully over PCA, it justifies investing remaining budget in multiprofile+scvi_n200 and multimodal scvi configurations; if not, we can pivot to scgpt or multiprofile aggregation with PCA. This is the cleanest single-variable comparison available and the best use of experiment 3 to reduce uncertainty about the most impactful design axis before committing to more complex multimodal or multiprofile configurations.

Evidence: scvi_n200 (0.5203) clearly outperforms pca_n2000 (0.4849) as an RNA encoder in singleprofile, and image-only (resnet50) is very weak (0.2079), confirming RNA as the dominant signal. The multiprofile dimension is completely untested. This experiment tests whether multiprofile with avgpool aggregation improves upon the best singleprofile RNA result using the strongest encoder (scvi_n200). It isolates the profile/aggregation effect on top of the best encoder, keeping the design simple (no transformer, no multimodal). If multiprofile+avgpool yields a meaningful gain over 0.5203, it justifies further investment in multiprofile variants (transformer, scgpt) in remaining experiments; if not, it redirects budget toward scgpt or multimodal fusion. With 6 experiments left, this is the highest-information single step to determine whether the profile dimension is worth exploiting.

Evidence: config_005 (rna_only, multiprofile, scvi_n200, avgpool) achieved 0.650 accuracy, a large jump over singleprofile scvi (0.520) and PCA (0.485), making it the clear best configuration so far. Image-only models are very weak (0.208), so the current priority is maximizing the RNA-only pipeline before considering multimodal fusion. Question: Does transformer aggregation outperform avgpool for multiprofile scvi_n200 representations? config_006 is a single-variable change (avgpool → transformer) that isolates the aggregation effect while holding model, profile, and encoder fixed. Why: This is the highest-value next step because it directly extends the strongest signal found, costs only one experiment, and if transformer aggregation helps, it establishes a stronger baseline for any subsequent multimodal experiments within the remaining 5-experiment budget.

Evidence: RNA-only models dominate (best: 0.653 with scVI n200, multi-profile, transformer), while image-only is very weak (0.208). The multi-profile + transformer setup with scVI n200 is our current best. Uncertainty: We have not yet tested whether scGPT, a different RNA encoder, could outperform scVI n200 in the multi-profile setting. This experiment (config_009: RNA-only, multi-profile, scGPT, transformer) directly compares to our best (config_006) by changing only the encoder, isolating that effect. This is the best use of the next slot because: (1) it reduces uncertainty about the most important remaining design choice (RNA encoder) before committing remaining budget to multimodal experiments, (2) if scGPT is superior, subsequent multimodal experiments should use it; if not, we confirm scVI as the backbone and can pivot to testing whether multimodal fusion adds value, and (3) it avoids the risk of 'wasting' an experiment on a multimodal config that might be dragged down by the weak image signal without first confirming we have the best RNA representation.

The current best is config_006 (RNA-only, multiprofile, scvi_n200, transformer) at 0.653. All RNA-only variants with weaker encoders (pca_n2000, scgpt) are clearly inferior, leaving little room for RNA-only refinement. The critical untested question is whether multimodal fusion can push beyond 0.653. Image-only resnet50 was very weak (0.208), but fusion with a strong RNA backbone may still extract complementary spatial information. I choose config_033 (multimodal, multiprofile, scvi_n200, resnet50, transformer, weighted) because: (1) it pairs the best-known RNA setup (scvi_n200 + multiprofile + transformer) with the image modality to directly test the fusion hypothesis; (2) weighted fusion is the safest choice given the uncertain image quality—it can learn to downweight a weak image signal rather than being forced to process it equally as with concat; (3) resnet50 is already characterized (0.208), making the multimodal result interpretable as a clean fusion effect; (4) with 3 experiments remaining, if this beats 0.653 we can immediately try ViT-L next, and if it does not, we confirm RNA-only is optimal and avoid wasting budget on further multimodal variants with a known-weak encoder.

The best result so far is config_033 (multimodal, multiprofile, scvi_n200, resnet50, transformer, weighted) at 0.713 accuracy. The key uncertainty is whether the image modality's contribution is limited by the relatively weak ResNet50 encoder (image-only ResNet50 scored only 0.208). Config_039 changes only the image encoder to imagenet_vit_l while keeping all other proven elements (scvi_n200, multiprofile, transformer aggregation, weighted fusion) identical to config_033. This isolates the effect of image encoder quality. If ViT-L's stronger pretrained visual features improve the multimodal result, it validates investing in a better image backbone; if not, it confirms the image modality's ceiling and we can focus remaining budget on RNA-side or fusion refinements. With 2 experiments left after this, a single-variable test on the most impactful untested dimension is the highest-value use of the next slot.

The best result so far is config_039 (multimodal, multiprofile, scvi_n200, imagenet_vit_l, transformer, weighted) at 0.7250 accuracy. The only untested variation within this exact architecture is the fusion method: config_038 swaps weighted fusion for concat while holding all other settings identical. This isolates the effect of fusion strategy with a single variable change. Given only 1 experiment remains after this one, exploiting the strongest configuration with the most targeted modification (fusion: weighted → concat) maximizes the chance of either finding a new best or confirming weighted fusion is optimal. All other options either change multiple variables simultaneously or explore directions (e.g., scgpt, resnet50, avgpool) that prior evidence suggests are inferior.

The current best is config_039 (multimodal, multiprofile, scvi_n200, imagenet_vit_l, transformer, weighted) at 0.7250. The evidence strongly supports scvi_n200, multiprofile, imagenet_vit_l, and weighted fusion. The one remaining untested variable in this optimal neighborhood is aggregation: transformer (config_039, 0.7250) vs. avgpool (config_037, untested). In the RNA-only setting, transformer marginally outperformed avgpool (0.6530 vs 0.6501), but the interaction with multimodal fusion is untested. As the final experiment, config_037 provides a clean single-variable comparison to the current best, clarifying whether the transformer aggregation contributes meaningfully in the multimodal context or whether the simpler avgpool is sufficient. If avgpool matches or approaches transformer, it confirms the aggregation is not a critical bottleneck; if it falls short, it validates the transformer choice. This is the most informative use of the last experiment slot given that all other design axes (encoder, profile, image backbone, fusion) have been well-characterized.
